scenes.title: From a sample to a result
headline: From a sample to a result
scenes.narration: In respiratory-virus testing, the hard question is how a sample becomes a reliable signal. This review examines several microfluidic approaches, not one validated commercial instrument.

scenes.title: The channel
headline: The channel
scenes.narration: A microfluidic channel directs a small amount of sample past defined sensing areas. Geometry changes transport and contact time, which can influence whether the target reaches the surface.

scenes.title: Capture is conditional
headline: Capture is conditional
scenes.narration: Different systems use antibodies, aptamers or magnetic beads to recognize targets. Binding alone does not guarantee specificity, particularly in complex nasal fluids.

scenes.title: Different light signals
headline: Different light signals
scenes.narration: An optical microchip may read fluorescence, absorption or a plasmonic change. The signal depends on the chosen chemistry, optics and background, not simply the presence of a virus.

scenes.title: Charge is another route
headline: Charge is another route
scenes.narration: Electrochemical or electrical sensors convert a local target-related event into an instrument signal. Surface fouling, ionic conditions and interfering compounds still matter.

scenes.title: RNA is not antigen
headline: RNA is not antigen
scenes.narration: Nucleic acid detection first has to make its intended viral sequence accessible. When amplification is used, contamination and assay controls become essential.

scenes.title: Every threshold has a cost
headline: Every threshold has a cost
scenes.narration: Detection limits, cross-reactivity and reproducibility must be measured with proper samples. A promising sensor prototype is not automatically a clinically validated point-of-care test.

scenes.title: The review's proper claim
headline: The review's proper claim
scenes.eyebrow: AN ENGINEERING MAP, NOT CLINICAL ADVICE
scenes.narration: The paper maps ways to engineer direct respiratory-virus detection. Choosing a device requires independent validation of sensitivity, specificity and practical use.
